note: Linux CI measurements of this checkout's engine over the frozen corpus v0.4.0: the tree at that tag, unpacked with git archive, with no vendor/bundle, so gems' own sig/ directories do not load (#1507). allocations is the tight signal; wall_s is a coarse backstop. Switched on 2026-09-27 from Rigor's own growing lib. The previous baseline (the v0.4.0 cut, run 36278383180) measured the v0.4.0 engine over the v0.4.0 checkout with its bundle: 42,721,526 allocations, wall_s 44.179, peak_rss_kb 563,060. Its +80.5% over v0.3.9 mixed a lib 26% larger with the engine's own +19.1% (#1469), and the band could not tell them apart. This run measures master d709a0419 (v0.4.0 plus #1491, #1496, #1508, #1509 and #1511) over the v0.4.0 tree: 38,543,742 allocations, wall_s 46.083, peak_rss_kb 584,384. The same engine read 38,586,535 allocations on macOS (+0.11%), and the two CI reps differed by 228 objects. Refresh on the same corpus after an engine improvement: trigger release-gate.yml on master, download the bench-baseline-* artifact and commit it here with a note. After each release, advance corpus to the new tag from a branch cut at the tag (the rigor-release-prep skill). Sampling rule (#987): each gate run takes 2 reps per target, EACH IN A FRESH PROCESS (VmHWM is a per-process high-water mark, so an in-process rep can never report lower RSS, and a warm rep's wall is not comparable with this cold baseline), and records the LOWER of the reps for wall_s and peak_rss_kb while allocations and diagnostics are taken from the first rep unreduced. Measure a recalibration the same way -- bench/baseline.updated.json is already reduced, so committing it preserves the rule.
